pred_reasoning_trace: A 62-year-old woman presents with 24 hours of fever, left-sided flank pain, and foul-smelling urine. Five years earlier she underwent bilateral lung transplantation for severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (FEV1 15%). Her past medical history is notable for hypertension and a 70–pack-year smoking history. Immunosuppressive therapy consists of prednisone and tacrolimus; mycophenolate mofetil was discontinued for leukopenia. Prophylactic antimicrobial therapy includes trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole, itraconazole, and valganciclovir (continued for detectable CMV viremia). On examination she is febrile but otherwise unrevealing. Laboratory studies show a leukocytosis of 20,000 per µL (neutrophils 18,150 per µL) and hyponatremia (122 mEq/L).
